programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona a' cur seachad an latha a' leantainn na faoileagan 's ag ionnsachadh ioma rud inntinneach mun na cleachdaidhean aca... fiosrachadh a tha air leth feumail nuair a thig Baba bochd a chur ann an cunnart! programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha tubaist aig Bernie a tha fàgail an t-slige aige briste! Tha Oona 's Silky a' cur romhpa slige ùr a lorg dha aig grunnd na mara ach chan e gnìomh furasta a th' ann dhaibh tè fhreagarrach fhaighinn! When Bernie has an accident and manages to break his shell, Oona and Silky volunteer to dive to the depths to find him a new one. However, it proves to be quite the challenge to find one suitable.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Fhad ’s a tha iad a-muigh a’ campachadh, tha seanair Pheicein ag innse sgeulachd dhan chloinn mu Each an Toileachais, a tha a’ fuireach sa choille sheunta. Tha a’ chlann a’ dol air chuairt dhan choille sheunta agus nuair a lorgas iad Each an Toileachais, tha iad ag ionnsachadh nach eil e idir mar a bu dùil. While they are out camping, Petit's grandpa tells the children the tale of the Happiness Horse that lives in the enchanted forest nearby. The kids head into the forest, and when they find the Happiness Horse, they discover that it is never how one imagines it.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-abadas ri geamannan turas eile 's feumaidh Seren a dhol a' lorg coimpuitar. Ach saoil an tig aice air a leithid a lorg am measg an uidheamachd eile a tha am broinn an taighe? The Abadas are playing 'Simon Says' when Seren goes looking for a computer. Will she be able to find it amongst all the electronic devices in the house?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Ruairidh Gray a’ leughadh An Aisling Mhòr aig Beag. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Manjeet Mann, a dhealbhachadh le Amanda Quartey agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. Ruairidh Gray reads An Aisling Mhòr aig Beag by Manjeet Mann, illustrated by Amanda Quartey and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha iomagain air an Rìgh ’son ’s gum bi Stella sàbhailt' nuair a thèid i a-mach aig meadhan-oidhch’ 'son an dùbhradh-gealaich fhaicinn. The King is worried for Stella’s safety when she goes out at midnight to see the lunar eclipse.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella air a gealladh a thoirt gun toir i taic le bhith coimhead às dèidh na piseig' ùr aig Mìcheal. Tha aice ri bhith sèolta ge-tà oir tha fios aice nach bi an Rìgh toilichte le seo seach gu bheil i fhèin ‘s e fhèin aileirdsig o chait. Stella has promised to help look after Mìcheal’s new kitten. She has to be cunning though as she knows the King won’t be happy - she and the King are both allergic to cats.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha Charlotte dà bhliadhna-dheug a dh’aois agus tha i à Cologne, sa Ghearmailt. Rugadh i às aonais làmh cheàrr is ged a tha seo a’ cur bacadh oirre, tha i misneachail dhi fhèin. Tha i airson a bhith na cleasaiche nuair a dh’ fhàsas i mòr. Charlotte is 12-years-old and she is from Cologne, in Germany. She was born without a left hand and, although this keeps her back, she is a positive person. She wants to be an actor when she grows up.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha Belle is Sebastian cho treun 's a bha ’ad a-riamh nuair tha Mitch, an sreapadair cliùiteach, san sgìre. Belle and Sebastian are as brave as ever when the famous climber, Mitch, is in the area.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha bana-charaid an Tuathanaich air tadhal, leis a' pheata aice na cois, rabaid bheag. Nuair a tha iad ag ithe lòn tha uallach air Bitzer coimhead às a dèidh ach gu h-obann tha i a' dol a-mach à sealladh. Tha Seonaidh 's an treud air tòir na rabaid mus mothaich duine gu bheil i air chall. Ach bheil fios aca dè tha iad a' lorg? The farmer's niece has come to visit, bringing her precious pet rabbit with her. The farmer entrusts Bitzer to look after it while they go inside for lunch. All in a day's work - until the rabbit disappears! Shaun and the flock are called into action to help track down the elusive pet before the niece discovers it's missing. But do they understand what they're looking for?

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Waffles - tha iad a’ còrdadh ris a’ mhòr-chuid de dhaoine. Tha Abigail gan dèanamh i fhèin agus gan sgeadachadh gu brèagha. Brunch gu math blasta a dh’fhàgas gu math làn thu. Waffles - most people love them. Abigail makes them from scratch and presents them beautifully. A very tasty and filling brunch. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Slighe Naoimh Cuithbeirt/St Cuthbert's Way
programme.desc: Iagan MacNèill a’leantail Slighe Naoimh Chuithbeirt a Monteviot gu Kirk Yetholm. Iagan MacNeil explores the St Cuthbert’s Way, from Monteviot to Kirk Yetholm.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay MacMahon walks with Calum Steele through the Perthshire countryside, along a reservoir and to the top of Innerdownie. He talks about family life and the importance his father had on him and the community. As they appreciate the nature surrounding them and discuss why they love the Scottish outdoors, Calum also reflects on his long career as a police officer and as general secretary of the Scottish Police Federation. Tha Ramsay a’ coiseachd tro dhùthaich Shiorrachd Pheairt, an cois tasgadh-uisge agus gu mullach Inbhir Dùnaigh cuide ri Calum Steele. Tha e a’ bruidhinn mu a bheatha teaghlaich agus a’ bhuaidh mhòr a bh’ aig athair air fhèin agus air a’ choimhearsnachd. A’ gabhail a-steach an àrainneachd nàdarrach mu thimcheall orra agus a’ bruidhinn mun ùidh a th’ aig an dithis ann a bhith a-muigh ann an Alba, tha Calum cuideachd a’ cnuasachdh air a dhreuchd fhada mar oifigear poilis agus mar Àrd-Rùnaire de Chaidreachas Poileas na h-Alba. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Prògram sònraichte a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn. A’ gabhail a-steach ceòl a choisinn cliù dhan chòmhlan agus agallamhan le Aonghas MacPhàil agus Andrew Stevenson. Air aithris le Megan NicGill-Fhaolain. A special programme to celebrate 25 years of Skipinnish, recorded at Edinburgh Castle in front of thousands of fans. The concert includes the music that made the band famous, and features interviews with members Angus MacPhail and Andrew Stevenson. Narrated by Megan NicGill-Fhaolain. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: An Cruinne Caochlaideach/Dynamic Planet
programme.desc: As Earth’s climate changes, the once-stable natural systems that we rely upon are being thrown into chaos.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Là 3 aig Belladrum 2025 agus Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air LUSA gu Àrd-Ùrlar a’ Ghàrraidh. A’ chiad turas aca aig Belladrum, ’s e pròiseact ùr iongantach a th’ ann an LUSA bhon riochdaire is cluicheadair synth, Innes Strachan, le cuid dhen luchd-ciùil as fheàrr an Alba. Còmhla, tha fuaim sònraichte aca agus measgachadh de cheòl electro-pop agus electronica synth. Day three at Belladrum and Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome LUSA to the Garden Stage. Marking their festival debut, LUSA is the exciting new project from producer and synth player Innes Strachan, who is joined onstage by some of Scotland’s top musicians. Together, they have a distinctive sound and their set list features a mix of electro-pop songs and synth driven electronica.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: An intimate portrait of a fiercely independent Hollywood star who left it all behind to live life on her own terms, revealing a haunting, resilient journey of art, identity and authenticity in the shadow of one of cinema’s most iconic roles.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo boards the West Highland Line to begin a railway journey across Scotland’s central belt, from the Arrochar Alps to the Loch of the Lowes. At the head of Loch Long, Michael meets a legendary octogenarian munro-bagger. In Balloch, on the shores of Loch Lomond, he joins passionate volunteers working to restore an iconic 1950s paddle steamer. In Glasgow, Michael rides the 'Clockwork Orange', the third oldest underground rail system in the world, to Govan and the shipyards of the River Clyde. And at Kelvinbridge, Michael hears how the chicken tikka masala was created for the Glaswegian palate by an immigrant chef from Lahore.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Nigel Farage has accused parts of the British media of mounting a politically-motivated campaign against him after reports about his financial interests prompted an investigation by Parliament's Standards Commissioner. Gabriel Pogrund, editor of the Insight investigations team at The Sunday Times, outlines the reporting behind their story, while journalist Michael Crick and Brendan O'Neill of Spiked discuss the political and journalistic issues. A High Court judgment has dismissed all claims brought by Prince Harry and six other claimants against Associated Newspapers over allegations that journalists used unlawful methods to obtain information. The ruling marks a significant moment in the long-running legal and political legacy of Britain's phone-hacking and press intrusion scandals. Susan Aslan, media lawyer, outlines the legal significance of the judgment.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. As the anniversary celebrations continue, Ben and Kate look back at the time a binturong mysteriously started refusing food, seriously worrying the keepers. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Elsewhere, the keepers celebrate an important milestone as a critically endangered white-backed vulture chick reaches a crucial stage in its development. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: A family home is targeted in an arson attack – and two people die. But the matches police found are damp and only give a partial DNA profile. There is nothing to put the main suspects at the scene until an eagle-eyed detective realises there is something wrong with the CCTV footage. Also, police hunting for a burglar who’s stolen hundreds of thousands of pounds' worth of jewellery get their moment of proof from a distinctive piece of clothing.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist uses modern DNA techniques to solve the cold case murder of Hilda Murrell, and cell site analysis helps place a suspect at the scene of Abdul Deghayes’s killing.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers buy a pair of cottages in north Norfolk and plan to create one stunning family home. Martel meets a developer in North Yorkshire, who puts his DIY skills to the test refurbishing a three-bedroom semi-detached house. In Somerset, Martin tours a tired terrace that has just five weeks to be transformed for new tenants.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine visits Hereford, a city closely linked to the military, to see a collection of Second World War vehicles, equipment and memorabilia. At The Bunker, she meets Colin and Kathryn Taylor, World War II enthusiasts and custodians of this living museum, to learn about the heroic work of the military police, field medics and the famous SAS. From the passenger seat of a restored Jeep and a Humber ambulance, Roo sees how Colin and Kathryn are helping to keep history alive. Over in Leominster, two teams of bargain hunters are on manoeuvres, seeking profitable antiques to take to auction. On team red are twin sisters Jo and Sarah with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team are father and daughter Bobby and Jas, with Richard Madley. With £300 in their pockets, Bobby and Jas spot a desktop barometer and thermometer set and decide it’s a fair-weather option for later. Across the antiques centre, Charles think he's seeing double when Jo picks up an art nouveau sculpture that he believes looks just like her! Up in Wrexham, auctioneer Matthew Tong casts a keen eye on the teams’ items before putting them under the hammer.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Hairdresser Mysteries
programme.desc: Hairdresser Lily Petal opens her new salon in the sleepy village of Blossom Vale, finding herself investigating a suspicious death and the theft of a valuable antique.

programme.title: Rick Stein's Australia
programme.desc: Rick travels to Australia's famous holiday hotspot Byron Bay. On his way, he takes a detour to the fishing town of Ballina, just south of the Byron Bay hinterland.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Returning home after eight years of living and working in Abu Dhabi, two teachers want to swap desert sand for the beaches of East Sussex, where Briony May Williams has the keys to what could be the couple’s new home. Keen to get involved in the local community, they visit the Bluebell Railway to see what volunteering opportunities there are on the heritage line.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Nigel Havers presides as members of the public with interesting items to sell come face to face with five dealers who bid against each other to try to bag themselves a bargain. Before facing the dealers, each seller has their item valued by auctioneer Simon Bower. Simon also gives them top tips on the history and key characteristics of their piece, so that when they enter the bidding room, they have all the information they need to try to haggle the best possible price from the dealers. All the dealers are spending their own money but have no idea what the sellers have brought in.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: Bee and Lauren help Emma downsize a home full of memories after losing her husband. Finding items full of stories in his home library, the family will turn his loss into legacy.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Gyles Brandreth. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Mark puts Lauren to the test, Vicki and Ross face another stumbling block, and Gina attempts to right a wrong.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.desc: The team help the Clarke family, whose home has been overwhelmed by the hobbies they love, leaving little room for everyday life.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction this week are guest panellists Harry Hill, Kojey Radical, Jill Scott and Stacey Solomon.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue’s husband Dave died two years ago, and now her only son, Michael, is moving out – again – to try to fix his marriage – again. But the good news is he has got Sue a surprise to help her live independently: an Ann Droid Z58/100 humanoid care robot. Sue really does not want a robot in her home, especially one that causes chaos straightaway. But is this robot actually the companion she most needs?

programme.desc: Austin misreads a dinner as a date, Julian battles a book title, and Ingrid debates betraying their motto 'No pair, no bear'.

programme.title: My Old Ass
programme.desc: In this coming-of-age fable, free-spirited teenager Elliott encounters her wisecracking 39-year-old future self and can’t escape her influence. On the cusp of leaving home for college, Elliott is determined to have one last summer packed with good times. To celebrate her 18th birthday, she boats off to a remote island with her best friends to trip on magic mushrooms. But just when Elliott thinks she’s not feeling a thing, she suddenly finds herself chatting with a woman who claims to be her literal 'old ass', the person she is apparently destined to become in two decades' time! Prodded for advice, Elliott’s future self gives her one major warning: avoid anyone named Chad, which sounds easy enough. But when Elliott meets the very Chad she was supposed to dodge, things get complicated. Elliott starts to open herself to what her future self might have to show her... and vice versa!

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. As the anniversary celebrations continue, Ben and Kate look back at the time a binturong mysteriously started refusing food, seriously worrying the keepers. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Elsewhere, the keepers celebrate an important milestone as a critically endangered white-backed vulture chick reaches a crucial stage in its development. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: A family home is targeted in an arson attack – and two people die. But the matches police found are damp and only give a partial DNA profile. There is nothing to put the main suspects at the scene until an eagle-eyed detective realises there is something wrong with the CCTV footage. Also, police hunting for a burglar who’s stolen hundreds of thousands of pounds' worth of jewellery get their moment of proof from a distinctive piece of clothing.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist uses modern DNA techniques to solve the cold case murder of Hilda Murrell, and cell site analysis helps place a suspect at the scene of Abdul Deghayes’s killing.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers buy a pair of cottages in north Norfolk and plan to create one stunning family home. Martel meets a developer in North Yorkshire, who puts his DIY skills to the test refurbishing a three-bedroom semi-detached house. In Somerset, Martin tours a tired terrace that has just five weeks to be transformed for new tenants.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine visits Hereford, a city closely linked to the military, to see a collection of Second World War vehicles, equipment and memorabilia. At The Bunker, she meets Colin and Kathryn Taylor, World War II enthusiasts and custodians of this living museum, to learn about the heroic work of the military police, field medics and the famous SAS. From the passenger seat of a restored Jeep and a Humber ambulance, Roo sees how Colin and Kathryn are helping to keep history alive. Over in Leominster, two teams of bargain hunters are on manoeuvres, seeking profitable antiques to take to auction. On team red are twin sisters Jo and Sarah with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team are father and daughter Bobby and Jas, with Richard Madley. With £300 in their pockets, Bobby and Jas spot a desktop barometer and thermometer set and decide it’s a fair-weather option for later. Across the antiques centre, Charles think he's seeing double when Jo picks up an art nouveau sculpture that he believes looks just like her! Up in Wrexham, auctioneer Matthew Tong casts a keen eye on the teams’ items before putting them under the hammer.

programme.title: My Old Ass
programme.desc: In this coming-of-age fable, free-spirited teenager Elliott encounters her wisecracking 39-year-old future self and can’t escape her influence. On the cusp of leaving home for college, Elliott is determined to have one last summer packed with good times. To celebrate her 18th birthday, she boats off to a remote island with her best friends to trip on magic mushrooms. But just when Elliott thinks she’s not feeling a thing, she suddenly finds herself chatting with a woman who claims to be her literal 'old ass', the person she is apparently destined to become in two decades' time! Prodded for advice, Elliott’s future self gives her one major warning: avoid anyone named Chad, which sounds easy enough. But when Elliott meets the very Chad she was supposed to dodge, things get complicated. Elliott starts to open herself to what her future self might have to show her... and vice versa!

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. As the anniversary celebrations continue, Ben and Kate look back at the time a binturong mysteriously started refusing food, seriously worrying the keepers. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Elsewhere, the keepers celebrate an important milestone as a critically endangered white-backed vulture chick reaches a crucial stage in its development. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: A family home is targeted in an arson attack – and two people die. But the matches police found are damp and only give a partial DNA profile. There is nothing to put the main suspects at the scene until an eagle-eyed detective realises there is something wrong with the CCTV footage. Also, police hunting for a burglar who’s stolen hundreds of thousands of pounds' worth of jewellery get their moment of proof from a distinctive piece of clothing.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist uses modern DNA techniques to solve the cold case murder of Hilda Murrell, and cell site analysis helps place a suspect at the scene of Abdul Deghayes’s killing.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers buy a pair of cottages in north Norfolk and plan to create one stunning family home. Martel meets a developer in North Yorkshire, who puts his DIY skills to the test refurbishing a three-bedroom semi-detached house. In Somerset, Martin tours a tired terrace that has just five weeks to be transformed for new tenants.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine visits Hereford, a city closely linked to the military, to see a collection of Second World War vehicles, equipment and memorabilia. At The Bunker, she meets Colin and Kathryn Taylor, World War II enthusiasts and custodians of this living museum, to learn about the heroic work of the military police, field medics and the famous SAS. From the passenger seat of a restored Jeep and a Humber ambulance, Roo sees how Colin and Kathryn are helping to keep history alive. Over in Leominster, two teams of bargain hunters are on manoeuvres, seeking profitable antiques to take to auction. On team red are twin sisters Jo and Sarah with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team are father and daughter Bobby and Jas, with Richard Madley. With £300 in their pockets, Bobby and Jas spot a desktop barometer and thermometer set and decide it’s a fair-weather option for later. Across the antiques centre, Charles think he's seeing double when Jo picks up an art nouveau sculpture that he believes looks just like her! Up in Wrexham, auctioneer Matthew Tong casts a keen eye on the teams’ items before putting them under the hammer.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Tommy Tiernan's Epic West
programme.desc: In the place he calls home, Tommy continues his journey along one of the world’s most evocative coastlines, bringing a visual feast and fitting tribute to the immense beauty, rich heritage and unique spirit of the west of Ireland. From the rocky silence of the Burren to the electronic world of a Galway nightclub, Tommy meets Blindboy Boatclub, Galwegian DJ Shampain and poet Mary O'Malley and looks at how the west inspires films, art and music. At times humorous and touching, this is an exploration of the west's epic crooked landscapes and the creativity they provoke. From romantic myths to harsh realities, Tommy takes us on a ramble through the Irish imagination in all its awkward contradictions.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Atlantic bluefin tuna, one of the largest fish in the sea, are making a surprise comeback off Northern Ireland’s coast, sparking an ambitious new vision for local fishing. Davy Frayne and Jonny Thursby, two anglers from the town of Ballycastle, have been fishing for giant bluefin tuna in the area for six years. Now they are attempting to establish a bluefin fishery, boasting catches of up to 1,000 pounds in weight. The stretch between Ballycastle and Rathlin is an unforgiving one, so Davy and Jonny are tested to their limits, fishing in waters where bad weather, strong currents and deep waters can create treacherous conditions. They are on the water at every opportunity, starting at the break of dawn and fishing until the light fades over the water to the west. Ballycastle is a town steeped in fishing history, where the people have longstanding connections with the waters. But in recent years, fleets have diminished and fish stocks have been low. Davy and Jonny are attempting to bring a new form of fishing to this coastline, one never seen before in these waters, and many sceptics doubt the viability of the project.

programme.title: Tommy Tiernan's Epic West
programme.desc: In the place he calls home, Tommy continues his journey along one of the world’s most evocative coastlines, bringing a visual feast and fitting tribute to the immense beauty, rich heritage and unique spirit of the west of Ireland. From the rocky silence of the Burren to the electronic world of a Galway nightclub, Tommy meets Blindboy Boatclub, Galwegian DJ Shampain and poet Mary O'Malley and looks at how the west inspires films, art and music. At times humorous and touching, this is an exploration of the west's epic crooked landscapes and the creativity they provoke. From romantic myths to harsh realities, Tommy takes us on a ramble through the Irish imagination in all its awkward contradictions.

programme.title: My Old Ass
programme.desc: In this coming-of-age fable, free-spirited teenager Elliott encounters her wisecracking 39-year-old future self and can’t escape her influence. On the cusp of leaving home for college, Elliott is determined to have one last summer packed with good times. To celebrate her 18th birthday, she boats off to a remote island with her best friends to trip on magic mushrooms. But just when Elliott thinks she’s not feeling a thing, she suddenly finds herself chatting with a woman who claims to be her literal 'old ass', the person she is apparently destined to become in two decades' time! Prodded for advice, Elliott’s future self gives her one major warning: avoid anyone named Chad, which sounds easy enough. But when Elliott meets the very Chad she was supposed to dodge, things get complicated. Elliott starts to open herself to what her future self might have to show her... and vice versa!

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. As the anniversary celebrations continue, Ben and Kate look back at the time a binturong mysteriously started refusing food, seriously worrying the keepers. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Elsewhere, the keepers celebrate an important milestone as a critically endangered white-backed vulture chick reaches a crucial stage in its development. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: My Old Ass
programme.desc: In this coming-of-age fable, free-spirited teenager Elliott encounters her wisecracking 39-year-old future self and can’t escape her influence. On the cusp of leaving home for college, Elliott is determined to have one last summer packed with good times. To celebrate her 18th birthday, she boats off to a remote island with her best friends to trip on magic mushrooms. programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. As the anniversary celebrations continue, Ben and Kate look back at the time a binturong mysteriously started refusing food, seriously worrying the keepers. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Elsewhere, the keepers celebrate an important milestone as a critically endangered white-backed vulture chick reaches a crucial stage in its development. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: A family home is targeted in an arson attack – and two people die. But the matches police found are damp and only give a partial DNA profile. There is nothing to put the main suspects at the scene until an eagle-eyed detective realises there is something wrong with the CCTV footage. Also, police hunting for a burglar who’s stolen hundreds of thousands of pounds' worth of jewellery get their moment of proof from a distinctive piece of clothing.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist uses modern DNA techniques to solve the cold case murder of Hilda Murrell, and cell site analysis helps place a suspect at the scene of Abdul Deghayes’s killing.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers buy a pair of cottages in north Norfolk and plan to create one stunning family home. Martel meets a developer in North Yorkshire, who puts his DIY skills to the test refurbishing a three-bedroom semi-detached house. In Somerset, Martin tours a tired terrace that has just five weeks to be transformed for new tenants.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine visits Hereford, a city closely linked to the military, to see a collection of Second World War vehicles, equipment and memorabilia. At The Bunker, she meets Colin and Kathryn Taylor, World War II enthusiasts and custodians of this living museum, to learn about the heroic work of the military police, field medics and the famous SAS. From the passenger seat of a restored Jeep and a Humber ambulance, Roo sees how Colin and Kathryn are helping to keep history alive. Over in Leominster, two teams of bargain hunters are on manoeuvres, seeking profitable antiques to take to auction. On team red are twin sisters Jo and Sarah with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team are father and daughter Bobby and Jas, with Richard Madley. With £300 in their pockets, Bobby and Jas spot a desktop barometer and thermometer set and decide it’s a fair-weather option for later. Across the antiques centre, Charles think he's seeing double when Jo picks up an art nouveau sculpture that he believes looks just like her! Up in Wrexham, auctioneer Matthew Tong casts a keen eye on the teams’ items before putting them under the hammer.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. As the anniversary celebrations continue, Ben and Kate look back at the time a binturong mysteriously started refusing food, seriously worrying the keepers. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Elsewhere, the keepers celebrate an important milestone as a critically endangered white-backed vulture chick reaches a crucial stage in its development. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: The Moment of Proof
programme.desc: A family home is targeted in an arson attack – and two people die. But the matches police found are damp and only give a partial DNA profile. There is nothing to put the main suspects at the scene until an eagle-eyed detective realises there is something wrong with the CCTV footage. Also, police hunting for a burglar who’s stolen hundreds of thousands of pounds' worth of jewellery get their moment of proof from a distinctive piece of clothing.

programme.title: Expert Witness
programme.desc: A forensic biologist uses modern DNA techniques to solve the cold case murder of Hilda Murrell, and cell site analysis helps place a suspect at the scene of Abdul Deghayes’s killing.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two brothers buy a pair of cottages in north Norfolk and plan to create one stunning family home. Martel meets a developer in North Yorkshire, who puts his DIY skills to the test refurbishing a three-bedroom semi-detached house. In Somerset, Martin tours a tired terrace that has just five weeks to be transformed for new tenants.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Roo Irvine visits Hereford, a city closely linked to the military, to see a collection of Second World War vehicles, equipment and memorabilia. At The Bunker, she meets Colin and Kathryn Taylor, World War II enthusiasts and custodians of this living museum, to learn about the heroic work of the military police, field medics and the famous SAS. From the passenger seat of a restored Jeep and a Humber ambulance, Roo sees how Colin and Kathryn are helping to keep history alive. Over in Leominster, two teams of bargain hunters are on manoeuvres, seeking profitable antiques to take to auction. On team red are twin sisters Jo and Sarah with their expert Charles Hanson. On the blue team are father and daughter Bobby and Jas, with Richard Madley. With £300 in their pockets, Bobby and Jas spot a desktop barometer and thermometer set and decide it’s a fair-weather option for later. Across the antiques centre, Charles think he's seeing double when Jo picks up an art nouveau sculpture that he believes looks just like her! Up in Wrexham, auctioneer Matthew Tong casts a keen eye on the teams’ items before putting them under the hammer.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Hidden away above the bat cave, conservationists are investigating a worrying decline in one of the park's rare native bat colonies. Numbers have fallen sharply, and there are fears another species may be threatening the next generation. As the team search for answers, they hope to discover whether the colony can recover before more bats are lost. As part of the show's silver anniversary celebrations, Ben and Kate revisit one of the most memorable stories from the past 25 years. The only option is an anaesthetic to try to get to the root of the problem, but with any procedure of this kind there is always a worry that the animal may never wake up. Megan McCubbin also joins the keepers to weigh the park's three male gorillas. With each weighing more than twice as much as the average adult man, it's no easy task getting them onto the scales.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out
programme.desc: The team help the Clarke family, whose home has been overwhelmed by the hobbies they love, leaving little room for everyday life.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon is back in the host’s chair for the award-winning comedy panel show, with Lee Mack and David Mitchell returning as the lightning-quick team captains. Each week, a stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal extraordinary stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Sorting the fact from the fiction this week are guest panellists Harry Hill, Kojey Radical, Jill Scott and Stacey Solomon.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue’s husband Dave died two years ago, and now her only son, Michael, is moving out – again – to try to fix his marriage – again. But the good news is he has got Sue a surprise to help her live independently: an Ann Droid Z58/100 humanoid care robot. Sue really does not want a robot in her home, especially one that causes chaos straightaway. But is this robot actually the companion she most needs?

programme.title: Austin
programme.desc: Austin battles cultural branding, Ingrid wrangles with her new star, and Julian accidentally talks their Big Bear actor into quitting.

programme.title: My Old Ass
programme.desc: In this coming-of-age fable, free-spirited teenager Elliott encounters her wisecracking 39-year-old future self and can’t escape her influence. On the cusp of leaving home for college, Elliott is determined to have one last summer packed with good times. To celebrate her 18th birthday, she boats off to a remote island with her best friends to trip on magic mushrooms. But just when Elliott thinks she’s not feeling a thing, she suddenly finds herself chatting with a woman who claims to be her literal 'old ass', the person she is apparently destined to become in two decades' time! Prodded for advice, Elliott’s future self gives her one major warning: avoid anyone named Chad, which sounds easy enough. But when Elliott meets the very Chad she was supposed to dodge, things get complicated. Elliott starts to open herself to what her future self might have to show her... and vice versa!

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: JJ Chalmers and Grado uncover the best holiday escapes in Scotland. However, it’s up to friends and families from all over Scotland to decide which escapes make it to the grand final. Scotland’s greatest waterfront escape is decided by Suzie and Shirley, two best friends from Edinburgh. These city slickers are like fish out of water when it comes to remote escapes, but they find themselves wowed by the contemporary Inverlonan bothies, a retreat on Davaar Island and The Boathouse on Arran.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Ayr, crewmates Sophie and Shelby are called to a critical incident involving a woman who has suffered a burst gastric ulcer and is losing pints of blood. The team must act fast to take their patient to resus, the part of a hospital reserved for the most serious emergencies. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based paramedic Andrew, technician Simon and student Matthew treat Patrick, who is displaying a range of worrying symptoms, including a worsening headache, a rash and a sensitivity to light. The team can’t rule out meningitis but encounter a queue of ambulances outside Aberdeen Royal Infirmary. As Patrick’s condition deteriorates, the crew must administer treatment in the back of the ambulance. In North Ayrshire, Pam and Robert of the Special Operations Response Team attend a road traffic collision involving mum Joanne and young daughter Iris. Robert has to treat the pair calmly and reassuringly as they cope with the immediate aftermath of the upsetting incident. And just outside Dundee, ambulance teammates Chloe and David are called to a local police station where a man is trying to calm himself after taking an overdose of base, a particularly potent form of crack cocaine.

programme.title: City Lights
programme.desc: A nostalgic look back at City Lights, the iconic sitcom that captured the spirit of 1980s Scotland. Featuring the writer, cast and the famous faces it inspired.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. The local park has gone downhill, and Winston has a plan that will improve it.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Alan’s off out, and Michelle has invited Beth, Cathy and Christine over for a Girls’ Night. Cathy sets the tone by downing shots, and the revelations soon flow about the annoying things their men do. But when Beth jokes about one of Christine’s annoying habits, Christine gets the hump. It takes Michelle and a negotiation over a cheese toastie for Christine to forgive Beth. With the tunes now on, the dancing begins, and for a moment it seems as though nothing could come between these women. They even get a bit emotional. And when the girls decide to watch a film, Cathy jumps in with the suggestion they stick on a porno.

programme.desc: Shereen Cutkelvin presents highlights from the TRNSMT 2026 weekend, including Two Door Cinema Club, Skye Newman, Jacob Alon, Perrie, Wolf Alice, CMAT, Becky Hill and headliners Kasabian.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: After many happy years of married life, Cheryl’s beloved husband Pete passed away just a few months ago. A great collector and skilled with his hands, Pete was affectionately known by his family as Mr Fixit. But sadly, after surviving a stroke at a young age, Pete went on to suffer several years of poor health, and many of his ambitious projects remain incomplete. Leaving behind a number of partly restored motor vehicles, as well as an overwhelming amount of potentially valuable toys and novelty items, it’s time for a fresh start. But for Cheryl, who also lost her mum last year, the task of clearing out is more than she can take right now. So, she’s asked auctioneer Izzie Balmer and restorer Robin Johnson to help her. It’s transport galore for Izzie and Robin as they uncover a Velocette bicycle, a tricycle, a boat and even a scratch-build 4x4. Robin turns his specialist skills to an early e-bike, while Izzie hunts for treasures inside. At auction, a Royal Albert County Rose tea, coffee and dinner service wows the crowds, selling for over £600, and all the money raised mounts up to be shared among Pete’s family. A fitting tribute to Mr Fixit.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben and Kate celebrate 25 years of friendship, animal stories and unforgettable moments on Animal Park, and revisit the extraordinary life of lioness Malaika.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus wants to impress the locals with a French version of the classic Sunday roast - but first, he needs the perfect poulet. He also gives a masterclass on how to portion a whole chicken and tries to find the best wine to accompany the dish. Later, Marcus finds out how the French enjoy their take on the sandwich. Baguette in hand, he hits the market stalls looking for inspiration.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall, Jodie Kidd, Jamali Maddix and Suzi Perry take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the grand final of the classic quiz where six contenders return to the black chair in a bid to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are British and Irish Lions tours in the 21st century, Princess Margaret, the Rocky films, Bletchley Park during the Second World War, Augustus Caesar and the BBC sitcom Extras.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Sheep farming couple Tim and Tanya have breathed new life into their Cotswold farm, ensuring that Tim’s young son has the chance to take on a viable business in the future. Their most ambitious venture was three years in the making: they have recently launched the UK’s first sheep’s milk vodka. However, at £60 per bottle, the challenge will be to sell it. Tim and Tanya have high hopes that they can reel in potential buyers for their artisan spirit at Blenheim Palace Food Festival, even before lunchtime! Meanwhile, Wye Valley-based brothers Matt and Kit are working round the clock collecting honey from 150 beehives and making it into sparkling mead. As a young family business, they rely on their own teamwork to make the dream work. They hope bottles will fly off their stall once people sample their modern take on this ancient drink. On top of that, creating a buzz at this prestigious event could bring them closer to landing a lucrative deal.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: Tom serves up more revelations from the world of hospitality. This time, his attention turns to street food, which is experiencing something of a boom when the industry is struggling. He meets the founders of a street food collective that brings togeter local traders with DJs and live music; an authentic Thai food outfit taking the leap to bricks and mortar; and a barbecue smokehouse in Cornwall that resolutely stays open all year round. And in Marlow, it’s the opening night of Tom’s own food festival, Pub in the Park.

programme.title: Land of the Lost Wolves
programme.desc: After spending four weeks camping out in the bitterly cold Cascade Mountains, wildlife cameraman Gordon Buchanan and a team of wolf experts discover that most of the pack have been killed by locals who live by the motto 'shoot, shovel and shut up'. But have any of the pack escaped unharmed? As the team chase exciting new leads, there is a glimmer of hope on the horizon.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Michael Baggott and Mark Stacey find some real gems among the bags and boxes to take to auction. There's a nautilus shell that lights up the saleroom and some Superman film memorabilia that goes sky high. And Paul Martin explores the history of one of Britain's most famous tourist attractions; Highgate cemetery.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Eniola Aluko, Phil Daniels, Nikita Kanda and Danny Miller take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Ever wonder if doom-scrolling is draining your joy? You’re not alone. The science says cutting smartphone use to just two hours a day could seriously boost your wellbeing – but actually doing it is another story. So Zoe Ball is in Kettering to share with busy beautician Lucie some clever digital detox tricks that could improve family life, reduce stress and even boost her brain power. Less scrolling, more living.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: The world’s greatest classical music festival gets under way live from the Royal Albert Hall, with works by Copland, Gershwin and Ravel. Petroc Trelawny and Georgia Mann guide us through a night of spectacular music-making to kick off the summer's Proms season. Copland’s landmark Fanfare for the Common Man opens, followed by Gershwin’s ever-popular An American in Paris, and Ravel’s bluesy Piano Concerto, performed by piano superstar Yunchan Lim. A world premiere by Josephine Stephenson starts the second half, followed by Finzi’s ode to the patron saint of music – For St Cecilia – with tenor Thomas Atkins. Dalia Stasevska conducts the BBC Symphony Orchestra, BBC Singers and BBC Symphony Chorus.

programme.title: Golf: The Open
programme.desc: Highlights from the second day of the 154th Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. World number one Scottie Scheffler defends the title he won in emphatically in 2025, and world number two Rory McIlroy looks to add a second Claret Jug to the second Green Jacket he won at the Masters in April. Southport local Tommy Fleetwood will have the support of the home crowd as he aims to land his first major title, fellow Englishman Matt Fitzpatrick hopes to cap a stellar season by becoming the Champion Golfer of the Year, while Justin Rose returns to the venue where he famously burst onto the scene back in 1998.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Insomnia
programme.desc: Psychological thriller. Detective Will Dormer, a veteran of the Los Angeles Police Department, temporarily escapes an internal affairs investigation that may ruin his career by travelling to Nightmute, Alaska, to investigate the murder of a 17-year-old girl. Evidence mounts up against a reclusive novelist, but the perpetual daylight of the summer months within the Arctic Circle wreaks sleep-depriving havoc on the detective's body clock and threatens his judgement.

programme.title: Morningside
programme.desc: In the run-down Toronto district of Scarborough, the lives of assorted residents are linked by the Morningside Community Centre, closing to be replaced by condominiums as part of encroaching gentrification. Personal struggles, relationships, jealousies and societal challenges are explored in a place where senseless gun violence is also on the rise. Tragedy is inevitable.

Evidence mounts up against a reclusive novelist, but the perpetual daylight of the summer months within the Arctic Circle wreaks sleep-depriving havoc on the detective's body clock and threatens his judgement.

programme.title: Morningside
programme.desc: In the run-down Toronto district of Scarborough, the lives of assorted residents are linked by the Morningside Community Centre, closing to be replaced by condominiums as part of encroaching gentrification. Personal struggles, relationships, jealousies and societal challenges are explored in a place where senseless gun violence is also on the rise. Tragedy is inevitable.

programme.title: Ambulance
programme.desc: Alan watches on as crewmates Tracey and Lauren help his wife Jean from the floor of their caravan. Alarm bells ring as checks reveal she is suffering from life-threatening sepsis.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie’s juggling college and family life, learning about teenage mental health, online pressures and autism - and how care reaches far beyond the classroom.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: After many happy years of married life, Cheryl’s beloved husband Pete passed away just a few months ago. A great collector and skilled with his hands, Pete was affectionately known by his family as Mr Fixit. But sadly, after surviving a stroke at a young age, Pete went on to suffer several years of poor health, and many of his ambitious projects remain incomplete. Leaving behind a number of partly restored motor vehicles, as well as an overwhelming amount of potentially valuable toys and novelty items, it’s time for a fresh start. But for Cheryl, who also lost her mum last year, the task of clearing out is more than she can take right now. So, she’s asked auctioneer Izzie Balmer and restorer Robin Johnson to help her. It’s transport galore for Izzie and Robin as they uncover a Velocette bicycle, a tricycle, a boat and even a scratch-build 4x4. Robin turns his specialist skills to an early e-bike, while Izzie hunts for treasures inside. At auction, a Royal Albert County Rose tea, coffee and dinner service wows the crowds, selling for over £600, and all the money raised mounts up to be shared among Pete’s family. A fitting tribute to Mr Fixit.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: Ben and Kate celebrate 25 years of friendship, animal stories and unforgettable moments on Animal Park, and revisit the extraordinary life of lioness Malaika.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus wants to impress the locals with a French version of the classic Sunday roast - but first, he needs the perfect poulet. He also gives a masterclass on how to portion a whole chicken and tries to find the best wine to accompany the dish. Later, Marcus finds out how the French enjoy their take on the sandwich. Baguette in hand, he hits the market stalls looking for inspiration.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Hugh Fearnley-Whittingstall, Jodie Kidd, Jamali Maddix and Suzi Perry take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games kitchen composter?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents the grand final of the classic quiz where six contenders return to the black chair in a bid to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are British and Irish Lions tours in the 21st century, Princess Margaret, the Rocky films, Bletchley Park during the Second World War, Augustus Caesar and the BBC sitcom Extras.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Sheep farming couple Tim and Tanya have breathed new life into their Cotswold farm, ensuring that Tim’s young son has the chance to take on a viable business in the future. Their most ambitious venture was three years in the making: they have recently launched the UK’s first sheep’s milk vodka. However, at £60 per bottle, the challenge will be to sell it. Tim and Tanya have high hopes that they can reel in potential buyers for their artisan spirit at Blenheim Palace Food Festival, even before lunchtime! Meanwhile, Wye Valley-based brothers Matt and Kit are working round the clock collecting honey from 150 beehives and making it into sparkling mead. As a young family business, they rely on their own teamwork to make the dream work. They hope bottles will fly off their stall once people sample their modern take on this ancient drink. On top of that, creating a buzz at this prestigious event could bring them closer to landing a lucrative deal.

programme.title: The Hidden World of Hospitality with Tom Kerridge
programme.desc: Tom serves up more revelations from the world of hospitality. This time, his attention turns to street food, which is experiencing something of a boom when the industry is struggling. He meets the founders of a street food collective that brings togeter local traders with DJs and live music; an authentic Thai food outfit taking the leap to bricks and mortar; and a barbecue smokehouse in Cornwall that resolutely stays open all year round. And in Marlow, it’s the opening night of Tom’s own food festival, Pub in the Park.

programme.title: Land of the Lost Wolves
programme.desc: After spending four weeks camping out in the bitterly cold Cascade Mountains, wildlife cameraman Gordon Buchanan and a team of wolf experts discover that most of the pack have been killed by locals who live by the motto 'shoot, shovel and shut up'. But have any of the pack escaped unharmed? As the team chase exciting new leads, there is a glimmer of hope on the horizon.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. Antiques experts Michael Baggott and Mark Stacey find some real gems among the bags and boxes to take to auction. There's a nautilus shell that lights up the saleroom and some Superman film memorabilia that goes sky high. And Paul Martin explores the history of one of Britain's most famous tourist attractions; Highgate cemetery.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Eniola Aluko, Phil Daniels, Nikita Kanda and Danny Miller take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Just One Thing
programme.desc: Ever wonder if doom-scrolling is draining your joy? You’re not alone. The science says cutting smartphone use to just two hours a day could seriously boost your wellbeing – but actually doing it is another story. So Zoe Ball is in Kettering to share with busy beautician Lucie some clever digital detox tricks that could improve family life, reduce stress and even boost her brain power. Less scrolling, more living.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: The world’s greatest classical music festival gets under way live from the Royal Albert Hall, with works by Copland, Gershwin and Ravel. Petroc Trelawny and Georgia Mann guide us through a night of spectacular music-making to kick off the summer's Proms season. Copland’s landmark Fanfare for the Common Man opens, followed by Gershwin’s ever-popular An American in Paris, and Ravel’s bluesy Piano Concerto, performed by piano superstar Yunchan Lim. A world premiere by Josephine Stephenson starts the second half, followed by Finzi’s ode to the patron saint of music – For St Cecilia – with tenor Thomas Atkins. Dalia Stasevska conducts the BBC Symphony Orchestra, BBC Singers and BBC Symphony Chorus.

programme.title: Golf: The Open
programme.desc: Highlights from the second day of the 154th Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. World number one Scottie Scheffler defends the title he won in emphatically in 2025, and world number two Rory McIlroy looks to add a second Claret Jug to the second Green Jacket he won at the Masters in April. Southport local Tommy Fleetwood will have the support of the home crowd as he aims to land his first major title, fellow Englishman Matt Fitzpatrick hopes to cap a stellar season by becoming the Champion Golfer of the Year, while Justin Rose returns to the venue where he famously burst onto the scene back in 1998.

programme.title: DIY Deadly with Steve Backshall
programme.desc: In this unprecedented time of lockdown there has never been a better time to learn about the wildlife around us, and Deadly 60 fans have been sending in their videos, photos and questions for Steve Backshall to answer. In this episode, Steve focuses on our parks and gardens. This green space may look pristine, but for wildlife it’s savannah, jungle and mountains all rolled in to one. And judging by CBBC’s most observant viewers, its packed full of deadly animals! Steve unravels the mystery of some blue eggs in a nest, explains how a spider uses camouflage and trickery to lure in its prey, and tells about a worm that isn’t a worm... it’s a lizard! In a DIY demo, Steve then shows us how to keep hedgehogs warm and toasty during winter by building a hibernation house. But that’s not all. The audience gets their chance to ‘beat Backshall’ in a 60-second quickfire round. The question is, how many can Steve get right before his time is up? We also learn that fox cubs are endearing alarm clocks, and why you wouldn’t want to wander around an Australian garden without a grown-up!

Steve unravels the mystery of some blue eggs in a nest, explains how a spider uses camouflage and trickery to lure in its prey, and tells about a worm that isn’t a worm... it’s a lizard! In a DIY demo, Steve then shows us how to keep hedgehogs warm and toasty during winter by building a hibernation house. But that’s not all. The audience gets their chance to ‘beat Backshall’ in a 60-second quickfire round. The question is, how many can Steve get right before his time is up? We also learn that fox cubs are endearing alarm clocks, and why you wouldn’t want to wander around an Australian garden without a grown-up!

Is this something Hedgley the hedgehog can help them with?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels go for a woodland walk to help Duggee look for a very special leaf when they hear the strangest noise. In the distance, they can see a funny shape. What is that noise? What is that shape? Maybe it's a monster? No, wait! It's only Hedgley the hedgehog, who has been trundling around the forest collecting all sorts of leaves and twigs on his spiky quills, which make him look and sound like a leafy monster.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: During a heavy summer storm, Bluey is determined to dam the water in the front yard.

She spots something in the murky depths - a huge rusty submarine lying across the reef, and a moustache on the bow that means it must belong to Grandmaster Glitch. What's worse, the sub is leaking oil!

Dee meets a cool cucumber, and we meet a very cute baby one. The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou

programme.title: Froglets

programme.desc: The Twirlywoos watch people using a lift in a building. Chickedy and Chick follow two people into the lift and go up high with them, waving to Great BigHoo and Toodloo. The Twirlywoos keep making the lift go high and low at speed. The people emerge from the lift feeling very dizzy. Back inside The Big Red Boat, it is time for fruit tea but the Fruit Tea Machine stays down low. Chickedy, Chick and Toodloo try to pull it up high, only for it to fall back down low again, so Great BigHoo has a go. The Fruit Tea Machine keeps going high and low with Chickedy and Chick holding onto the spout! Eventually, the Fruit Tea Machine springs up so high it flies up out of the top of the boat, surprising the Quacky Birds!

Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are cardboard boxes which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate cardboard boxes inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘The Wheels on the Bus!’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

There is a lot of stuff to carry out before they can clean up, and some of it is very interesting. The Squirrels work hard but when they finish they can't find Duggee. Oh! The Squirrels have built a maze out of all the things in Duggee's workshop. Duggee is right in the middle of the maze, but can the Squirrels find the right way in? And once they're in, can they find the way out again?

Chantelle and Rory’s fact files help explain all of James's questions. With the help of the Teeny Tiny Creatures poem, we discover that, like lots of other teeny tiny creatures, earwigs are superheroes and help our planet in their own special way. In the Teeny Tiny Task, Rory, Sandy and Zoe play at being earwigs by using their pincer litter pickers to pick up leaves!

They head to where he was last seen, and a friendly owl helps Dan find his scent. Dan follows the scent and thinks he has found him – until another Eddie steps out of their tent. Dan has found some campers instead - can his super nose find another scent and track down the real Eddie?

Simon and Waffle put on a show for their excited guests, performing the amazing tricks Waffle has mastered. Next to arrive is Mr Meagre and his talking parrot, Pickles. Georgia gives birth to baby GiGi, but there is no time to rest as she has a wedding in Mallorca to plan - having enlisted 11 bridesmaids, Georgia meets with a designer to see the first draft of the dresses. The designer is also making her second party dress - with a tight corset, she is determined to lose her baby weight for her big day. Nathan encourages him to try and settle the court case once and for all so he can be present for Georgia in the lead-up to the wedding, but there's no stopping Georgia and it is full steam ahead as she continues with her wedding prep and sets off for a hen do in Ibiza while leaving the kids and Tommy behind for a three-day extravaganza.
